source_text: Quod si neutrum horum quae diximus, facies; et huic Deo te asseris credere, cuius institutis iniustitiam communiri aestimas; cognosce, multo te novum antiquo Manichaeo esse peiorem, qui talem Deum habeas, qualem Manichaeus Dei sui est commentus inimicum.
pass_a_gloss: Which if you will do neither of these things which we have said; and you assert that you believe this God, by whose institutes you estimate injustice to be fortified; recognize that you, a new one, are much worse than the old Manichaean, you who have such a God as the Manichaean invented as the enemy of his own God.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: If you will do neither of the things we have stated, and assert that you believe in this God whose ordinances you suppose to establish injustice, recognize that you, a new Manichaean, are far worse than an old one. Your God is of the very character that the Manichaean invented for the enemy of his God.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Opposite of iustitia; Julian refuses a God whose ordinances establish injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
